title: Cohort retention readout for January signups
scenario: January 2026 New-Year cohort signed up at 2.4× the December baseline. By week 8, 61% have stopped attending classes, vs 42% for the December cohort. You owe a retention readout for the leadership review: what's the same, what's structurally different about this cohort, and which 2 levers (not 12) would actually move the needle on week-12 retention.
badPrompt: write a cohort retention analysis for cult.fit january signups
badOutput:
Cohort Analysis: January 2026

The January cohort showed strong initial signups but lower retention compared to December. Possible reasons include New Year resolutions wearing off, schedule conflicts, and engagement issues. Recommendations: improve onboarding, add reminders, enhance class variety.

hints.title: Force structural differentiation
hints.body: ‘What's structurally different about this cohort, not just bigger.’ Without this, AI rehashes generic retention causes.

hints.title: Lock the lever count
hints.body: ‘2 levers, not 12. Argue why these two beat the others.’ Decision-grade memos don't list everything.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a retention readout.
Anchor the metric, cohort retention, week-8 attendance.
Anchor the cohort, January 2026 New-Year, 2.4× signup volume.
Use the actual numbers, 61% vs 42%, week 8.
Force structural differentiation, what's different, not just bigger.
Lock the count, 2 levers, with reasoning for why these beat the others.
Demand reasoning for why these two levers beat alternatives.
Specify sections, same / structurally different / 2 levers.

tipIfLow: Retention analyses get rehashy because LLMs reach for generic causes. The unlock is forcing structural differentiation (what's different about THIS cohort) and locking the lever count to 2 with explicit reasoning for why those two.
goldPrompt: You're a retention analyst. I'm Ishita at cult.fit. January 2026 New-Year cohort signed at 2.4× December baseline; 61% have stopped attending by week 8 (vs 42% for December). Output: (1) 'What's the same' vs December — 3 bullets, (2) 'What's structurally different' — 4 bullets with hypothesised mechanisms, NOT generic causes, (3) 'Two levers (not 12)' to move week-12 retention. For each lever, argue why it beats two alternatives I'd otherwise reach for. Refuse to list more than 2 levers.
